exposure: judicious use of oxytocin augmentation protocol
cohort: 20,227 women with singleton pregnancies ≥ 37 weeks gestation, cephalic presentation, spontaneous or induced onset of labor, and no previous cesarean section, delivering at Stavanger University Hospital, Norway, from 2009 to 2013
finding: Implementation of a judicious oxytocin augmentation protocol reduced overall oxytocin use, emergency cesarean sections, and umbilical artery pH < 7.1, but increased labor duration and severe postpartum hemorrhage.
mod_finding: Judicious use of oxytocin augmentation protocol was associated with a reduced frequency of emergency cesarean sections.
